rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Internal dialect never lands on a slide.
Emphasis budget — bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: chunk 3 "It answers in essays": line 23: "**Never let the agent say everything.**" — bolds a whole standalone six-word sentence (own capital + terminal period), not a ≲5-word handle sub-span. theory-plan.md's canonical spec (cited by this rule) reads: "Bold the handle (≲5 words, a sub-span of the sentence; never the whole lead sentence)." Contrast with the same file's compliant handles at lines 8 and 15 (**sycophancy**, **cascading error**), each a single coined-term word inside a longer sentence, not a sentence unto itself. The file's own maintainer note (line 36) calls this a 'Handle... bolded at naming moment' but the shape doesn't fit the sub-span/short-noun mold the rule defines — it reads as a bolded imperative maxim, not a coined term.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Either shrink the bold to a short sub-span inside a longer sentence (a coined 2-3 word handle) or drop the bold and let the sentence carry the point in plain narrative prose, consistent with the rest of the file's mechanism bullets.
